question.problem:
Consider the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 9 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
